items.title: James "Sing" Miller Interview, 1971-01-17
items.q: Kim was on a left hand banjo play, I've seen. Kim was left handed too but he writes right handed.

ctx.x: Is he musically inclined in any way?

Well, he had a thing that go on one time. But I don't know, he got the devil in him, you know, try to buy a house. That got away from him. He tried to play piano but I told him, you know, I said I never seen a left hand piano play yet, man. I've never seen a left hand piano play, man. I've seen a right hand piano play, you know. I never seen a... Kim was on a left hand banjo play, I've seen.

Well, Sylvester Handy is based... He's left handed but he... The way he plays it, he puts his right hand around backwards somehow or other. You notice? He plays left handed because he's left handed but it's the way he holds the strings by twisting his hand around.
